text:
sarah: FYI CS: acme saw 503s for ~10m during an authenticated batch job. Customer says calls started failing right after a scheduled model swap. They hit our hosted API with toolcalls and auth tokens.
ops-bot: alert: upstream-runner-eviction spike on pool gpu-a-2 (alert id: alert-1717532100) :rotating_light:
jordan: Can you paste the root error from the runner logs and a sample request they used? Need the model + batch size + auth pattern.
sarah: Pasting the log tail we got from support bundle. Customer says they were using model redwood/rlhf-large with toolcalls and embedding prefetch.
lin: ```
[2024-06-02T14:01:12Z] runner[pid=3421] ERROR: killed by SIGKILL (oom-killer)
[2024-06-02T14:01:12Z] kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 3421 (runner) total-vm: 124G, anon-rss: 84G, file-rss: 0K, shmem-rss: 0K
[2024-06-02T14:01:11Z] nvml: GPU 0: processes: pid 3421 size 78G
[2024-06-02T14:01:11Z] infer: context_size=4096 seq_len=2048 batch=24 concurrent_toolcalls=3
```
kyle: Hmm batch=24 + seq=2048 on that instance profile is above our safe mem curve for the quantized runtime. That combined with toolcall arg caching could expand KV state.
eric: Also seeing repeated "segfault@0x7ff..." right before the oom, likely memory corruption or double-free on prefetched KV.
nina: I've told the customer we're investigating and suggested a temporary retry/backoff. They asked for an ETA on a fix and if there's a workaround to avoid billing spikes.
jordan: Can we reproduce locally? lin/kyle — can you run the following repro (low risk) against a staging runner:
```bash
# simulate their request mix (auth + toolcall heavy)
for i in $(seq 1 50); do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <rotated-token>" \
    -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
    -d '{"model":"redwood/rlhf-large","input":"<long prompt>","max_tokens":1024,"tool_calls":[{"name":"lookup","args": {"q": "$(printf '%s' "$(yes 'big-arg' | head -n 500 | tr -d '\n')")"}}]}' &
done
wait
```
lin: I ran it in staging with batch=12 and concurrency=10 and reproduced a crash after ~60 s. Stacktrace points to kv_prefetch.c line 412 (grow_kv_cache) — allocation spike.
sarah: Customer also reported a billing anomaly where retries caused duplicate charge events; they have a large volume job so that got amplified. CS wants a temporary mitigation to avoid further charges.
kyle: Short-term mitigations: 1) route the customer's traffic to a smaller concurrency class (set per-customer conn cap) 2) enable per-request toolcall-size-limit (10k chars) 3) pin them to an older model variant (rlhf-medium) until we resolve. We can implement 1 & 2 as traffic-policy overrides in Console.
eric: I'll open a low-latency rollback: revert the last quantization/optimizer that landed yesterday on pool gpu-a-2. Might reduce memory pressure.
nina: I'll ask CS to apply the routing override and offer credit for duplicate bill events; they're OK to move while we triage.
jordan: Action items:
- lin: capture heap profile + core dump (if safe) from a repro node (ETA 30m)
- kyle: add a temporary per-customer conn cap & toolcall-size limit for acme (ETA 15m)
- eric: stage rollback of quant change on gpu-a-2 and monitor (ETA 45m)
- sarah/nina: coordinate customer comms and billing credit path (ETA 10m)
Please paste the heap profile link here when ready.
lin: Started sampling with pprof; uploading link to artifacts now: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/1717532100/kv-heap-profile.pb.gz
ops-bot: deploybot: rolled back commit 5f2b3a on pool gpu-a-2 (initiated by eric)
lin: After rollback and applying conn cap in staging, I re-ran the repro loop and did not see the OOM after 10 minutes. Reproducer uses unusually large tool args which previously triggered KV growth.
jordan: Good. We'll keep the mitigation in place for 24h and work on a proper fix in runtime: explicit KV eviction on toolcall boundary + stricter allocation accounting.
sarah: CS has approved the credit. Customer accepted routing to lower-concurrency pool and is paused on heavy jobs. Marking customer impact resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
eric: follow-up: open ticket with drivers team to check for any nvml leaks, and add a guard in runner to refuse toolcall payloads > 50k bytes (defense-in-depth).
lin: filing runtime PR with kv eviction + allocation cap. linking PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/985
nina: I'll close the support P1 once billing is cleared and customer confirms.
